sermon.title: Redeemer
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer teaches redemption from Israel’s deliverance out of Egypt, a parable of Christ. He walks through biblical servanthood—theft, debt, poverty, six-year limits, the death penalty for kidnapping—and the servant who said “I love my master.” We are redeemed from sin’s slavery to serve Jesus forever, bought with a price, and sent to open others’ eyes.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: “Exodus 20:23” spoken for Exodus 22:3; “Exodus 20:15” unclear; “eye for an eye” said to concern servants (Exodus 21:26–27 frees an injured servant); his account of runaway servants and courts; “the Bible never approved forced slavery” (compare Leviticus 25:44–46); about 2.5 million with hundreds of thousands of Egyptians in the exodus; resurrection body “without blood.” Unverified: over a million children abused, 600,000+ sexually abused yearly. Sensitive content kept as spoken: President Obama said to claim the Bible advocates slavery and called head of homosexual activists; homosexuals going to hell and “back in the closet”; Jesus’ priority not helping the poor.

chunks.section_question: What does it mean that God redeemed Israel?
chunks.short_answer: To redeem is to pay a ransom, rescue and deliver. Deuteronomy 13:5: the Lord brought you out of Egypt and redeemed you out of the house of bondage. Deuteronomy 26:8: with a mighty hand, great terribleness, signs and wonders—ten plagues, ending with the death of Egypt’s firstborn as the ransom.

faqs.question: What does “redeem” mean?
faqs.answer: To pay a ransom, rescue and deliver.

faqs.question: Who paid the ransom for Israel?
Did Jesus really die on the cross?
faqs.answer: His body died, but his spirit lived—just as ours will.

faqs.question: Why did Israel make thieves work rather than imprisoning them?
faqs.answer: Prison takes away the provider of the home.

faqs.question: How long did a Hebrew servant serve?
faqs.answer: Six years; in the seventh he went free.

faqs.question: Is Jesus just our Redeemer?
faqs.answer: He must also be Lord, whom we obey.

faqs.question: Did the law allow kidnapping people into slavery?
Is it impossible to keep his commandments?
faqs.answer: No—God gives the power to fulfill his word in us.

faqs.question: Are we our own?
faqs.answer: No—we are bought with a price.

faqs.question: Was Jesus’ priority to help the poor?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus came to save sinners, not alleviate poverty.
